title: Salade Nicoise
subtitle: A composed French salad with tuna, eggs, green beans, and olives
excerpt: Tinned tuna, soft-boiled eggs, crisp green beans, potatoes, tomatoes, and black olives arranged on a platter and dressed with a sharp vinaigrette. No mixing, just arranging.
sourceNotes: Classic salad from Nice and the surrounding Cote d'Azur region of France.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Cook the potatoes, eggs, and green beans up to one day ahead. Refrigerate separately and assemble just before serving.

content.text: A Nicoise is a composed salad, meaning each component sits in its own section on the platter rather than being tossed together. Cook every element separately and dress at the last moment so nothing wilts or goes soggy.
Cook the new potatoes in salted boiling water for 15 to 18 minutes until just tender. Drain and leave to cool, then halve.
Bring a separate pan of salted water to the boil. Lower the eggs in gently and cook for exactly 7 minutes. Transfer to cold water. Peel once cool and halve.
Blanch the green beans in the same boiling water for 3 minutes until just tender but still bright green. Drain and rinse under cold water to stop cooking.
Whisk the olive oil, red wine vinegar, mustard, garlic, salt, and pepper together in a small bowl until combined.
Arrange the lettuce leaves over a large serving platter as a base.
Place each component in its own section on the platter. Keep the tuna, eggs, potatoes, beans, tomatoes, olives, and anchovies separate.
Spoon the dressing over everything just before serving. Bring the platter to the table and let people serve themselves.

items.symptom: The egg yolks are fully set rather than soft.
items.cause: The eggs cooked longer than 7 minutes.
items.fix: Time carefully from when the eggs go in. Remove into cold water immediately at 7 minutes.

items.symptom: The green beans are drab and olive-coloured.
items.cause: They were not refreshed in cold water after blanching.
items.fix: As soon as they are drained, spread them on a tray and run cold water over them until completely cool.

items.cause: The vinegar ratio is high relative to the oil.
items.fix: Add another tablespoon of olive oil and a pinch of sugar to balance.
